newsitem.title: USA: Calif. agency says utility oversight reform needed.
newsitem.headline: Calif. agency says utility oversight reform needed.

text.p: An independent California commission has recommended that oversight of the state's electric and natural gas utilities be transferred to the Energy Commission rather than the Public Utilities Commission

In a report to be submitted to Governor Pete Wilson and the California Legislature, the Little Hoover Commission said the state needs to fundamentally reform its oversight of public utilities given the emergence of competition in the energy and telecommunications markets.
Currently the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) oversees a wide range of investor-owned monopoly utilities including electric, natural gas, water, telecommunications and railroads.

But the five CPUC commissioners have "an excessive work load" and should focus efforts on ushering competition into the telecommunications industry, said Jeannine English, executive director of the Little Hoover Commission.
In addition, deregulation of energy and telecommunications markets will mean the CPUC's traditional rate-setting role will no longer be needed, the report said.

The commission report also calls for oversight of water and transportation issues to move to other state agencies, while the PUC's energy efficiency activities should be transferred to the Department of Conservation.
